name: Peterson Hall
use: Medium co-ed residence hall (203 students), first-year and upper-division; Life Sciences learning community
style: Neo-traditional brick residence hall with cast-stone bands and gabled roofs (from photos)

facts.text: Built as SERC B (Southeast Residence Complex), opened 2007; renamed Peterson Hall on October 11, 2013.

SERC was a three-building complex for 730 students built by Harvey Construction to designs by JSA, Inc.; SERC B is about 52,000 sq ft. Harvey first demolished nine existing two-storey buildings on the site; Phase 1 (A and B) finished by summer 2007, Phase 2 (C) by summer 2008.
Housing lists 203 students; traditional pods and suites: 32 traditional doubles, 8 traditional singles, 24 suites of two doubles and 5 suites of two doubles and two singles.

All rooms air-conditioned; each of five floors has a large open lounge and a study lounge; first floor has a kitchen, laundry and recreation lounge. Elevator, automatic front door, roll-in showers in some suites.
Hosts the Life Sciences Residential Learning Community on floors 3 and 4 (traditional rooms).
Named for Walter R. Peterson, NH governor 1969-73 and UNH interim president 1995-96.

verdict: The smallest 2007 SERC hall: air-conditioned, accessible, standard rooms, generic brick.
notes: No licensed photo found. Reference photo: brick entrance canopy on square brick piers, cast-stone bands, same vocabulary as Handler. No reviews specific to Peterson found; old row's TNH "hotel feel" and closed-suite-door comments were not re-verified.
